title: Income and Wealth Inequality in Nigeria: Trends and Drivers (Oxfam in Nigeria / CISLAC / TJNA / CARE Nigeria report & policy brief, 15 October 2024)
notes: Two lead authors (Henry Ushie, Chinedu Bassey), eight contributing authors (John Makina, Regina Afiemo, Kwesi Obeng, Christian Hallum, Martin Brehm Christensen, Anthony Kamande, Francis Agbere, Jonas Gielfeldt), foreword endorser Hussaini Abdu (Country Director, CARE International in Nigeria), plus Oxfam in Nigeria and CARE International in Nigeria.

title: Taxing the Rich: Nigerian Fair Tax Monitor Thematic Report (TJNA / CISLAC / Oxfam in Nigeria / Oxfam Novib / Make Tax Fair, 15 October 2024)
notes: Lead author Mtwalo Msoni (TJNA), editors/reviewers Ishmael Zulu (TJNA), Martin Brehm Christensen (Oxfam Novib), and Henry Ushie (Oxfam in Nigeria), plus commissioning/partner organisations CISLAC (led by Auwal Musa Rafsanjani), Tax Justice Network Africa, Oxfam Novib, Make Tax Fair, and Tax Justice and Governance Platform.

title: Davos 2023 Inequality Report Abuja press briefing panel (Oxfam in Nigeria & Connected Development, 16 January 2023)
notes: Abuja press briefing unveiling Nigeria-specific wealth tax estimates ($3.2bn/year from 2%/3%/5% progressive wealth tax on fortunes above $5m/$50m/$1bn): Vincent Ahonsi, Regina Afiemo, Hamza Lawal (Connected Development), Kenneth Akpan, and Henry Ushie.

title: Blakey's National Tax Conference: Wealth Taxation in Nigeria — A Veritable Tool for Sustainable Development (Lagos, 5 February 2024)
notes: Pro-bono conference organised by Chartered Accountant Chief Blakey Okwudili Ijezie at Pholax Hotel & Suites, Anthony Village, Kosofe LGA, Lagos, with presentations by Pastor Felix Jarikre and Dr Tunji Adeniyi, reported by Vanguard columnist Sunny Ikhioya and citing Ben Akabueze and Doyin Salami.

title: Equity and digitisation in the property tax system in Lagos: A win-win for all? (African Cities Research Consortium, 19 December 2025)
notes: Four Nigerian academic co-authors (Esther Thontteh, Damilola Agbalajobi, Olumuyiwa Adegun, Taibat Lawanson) advocating progressive Lagos Land Use Charge reform, vacant land taxation, and land-value capture on wealthier landowners.

title: Joint Nigeria wealth-tax revenue model in Taxing the Rich (IPS, Oxfam, Fight Inequality Alliance, and Patriotic Millionaires)
notes: International coalition cited in the Nigerian Fair Tax Monitor report for estimating that a 2%/5%/10% progressive annual wealth tax on Nigerian fortunes above $5m/$50m/$1bn would raise over $6 billion (N4.59 trillion) annually.

title: Inheritance Tax and Wealth Redistribution in Nigeria (IJNRD Vol. 9 Issue 4, April 2024)
notes: Peer-reviewed accounting study by Abdulganiyu Babayanju (University of Abuja) and Rasheed Olatunji Animasaun (Crescent University, Abeokuta) recommending that the Nigerian government institute an inheritance tax to redistribute wealth.

title: Property Tax Reform in Nigeria: Comparative Insights from Three States (LoGRI & African Centre for Tax and Governance, November 2025)
notes: Joint study by African Centre for Tax and Governance (ACTG) and LoGRI (Regan McCort, Mustapha Ndajiwo, Timothy Onechojon Usman, and Michael Falade) advocating progressive property taxation as a wealth capture mechanism in Nigerian states.

title: Inequality in Nigeria: Exploring the Drivers (Oxfam International & Oxfam in Nigeria, 17 May 2017)
notes: Foundational Oxfam Nigeria inequality report authored by Emmanuel Mayah, Dr Chiara Mariotti, Evelyn Mere, and Celestine Okwudili Odo.
